subject.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel

question: Should OpenClaw establish `toolBindings` as a general external plugin-tool context contract, or should this browser-copilot binding remain owner-specific behind a typed browser/plugin seam?
rationale: The branch introduces a compatibility-sensitive plugin API surface for a security binding; source review cannot determine the permanent public SDK direction.

options.title: Define a typed plugin contract
options.body: Document and version the run-binding surface, validate it at the Gateway and plugin boundary, and add focused compatibility coverage.

options.title: Keep the binding browser-owned
options.body: Move the browser binding through a browser-specific injected runtime seam so unrelated plugins do not receive an opaque new context field.

options.title: Pause the API expansion
options.body: Land no general plugin context contract until maintainers decide whether other plugins need this capability.

recommendation.title: Define a typed plugin contract
recommendation.body: Document and version the run-binding surface, validate it at the Gateway and plugin boundary, and add focused compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR and authored the proposed contract and browser/Gateway integration.
